title: Derived-complete module complexes are closed under products and triangles
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $I\subseteq A$ be any ideal, and work in $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived completeness means [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex]. (1) If $(K_n)_{n\geq1}$ is a countable family of derived $I$-complete objects, its product $\prod_{n\geq1}K_n$ [def-weil-category-product] is derived $I$-complete. (2) In any distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ [def-weil-triangulated-category], if two of $X,Y,Z$ are derived $I$-complete, so is the third. These assertions require neither finite generation of $I$ nor boundedness of the complexes.

proof.text: Products of modules are exact even with independent ring and module universes: the forgetful functor to abelian groups preserves kernels and epimorphisms, hence homology and finite colimits, and reflects finite colimits. Pull exact countable products back along it. Apply [lem-weil-derived-countable-products-existence] to obtain countable products in D(A). This is the private Lean lemma module_countableAB4Star followed by derivedCategory_hasCountableProducts.

Fix f in I and write t_K = 1-s_f on the countable power of K [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. By TR1 and inverse rotation [def-weil-triangulated-category], t_K occurs as the second morphism of a distinguished Roos triangle L -> product K -> product K -> L[1]. Its first object is zero if and only if the second morphism is invertible (Mathlib Triangle.isZero1_iff_isIso2, from Hom exactness [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact]). Thus [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex] is equivalent to invertibility of every t_K. In the forward direction use one Roos triangle; in the reverse direction apply the same zero/isomorphism equivalence to each triangle quantified by the definition. This is complete_iff_isIso and uses no arbitrary witness to define data.

For K = product_i K_i let gamma_i : product_n K -> product_n K_i be the componentwise projection [def-weil-category-product]. Naturality [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism] gives t_K;gamma_i = gamma_i;t_Ki. Each t_Ki is invertible by the preceding step. Define q by its (n,i) component gamma_i;t_Ki^{-1};pr_n. The two product universal properties give q;gamma_i = gamma_i;t_Ki^{-1}; the family gamma_i is jointly monic by applying product extensionality twice. Consequently t_K;q and q;t_K both have composites gamma_i, and hence both are identities. Thus t_K is invertible, proving completeness of the product. This is the explicit private proof tower_isIso_product.

For a distinguished triangle T, its countable power P is distinguished by [lem-weil-pbc-products-distinguished-triangles]. Since shifts are A-linear, f times the identity is a triangle endomorphism of T. Let tau be the endomorphism of P with nth component pr_(n+1);(f times identity_T). Then phi = identity_P - tau has components exactly t_T.obj1, t_T.obj2 and t_T.obj3 by their definitions. Apply [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] to phi : P -> P for each pair of invertible components. The zero/isomorphism criterion in step 2 gives all three completeness implications. No localization module, tensor-product comparison, or auxiliary shift-stability theorem is needed.
